Dear Luis,

At the little fundraiser at No. 8 last week there was a pear cake, rather damp in the middle, which I enjoyed standing up between the umbrella stand and a bowl of those toothbrushes that people pretend not to take.  I asked the young man cutting it what was in it and he said pears with the confidence of somebody who has never baked anything.  These were not slices laid on top for show.  They were almost dissolved into the cake by the time you found them.

You went back for another bit, unless that was a man with your coat, so I thought I would write to you before commandeering somebody at the practice.  Was there a recipe slip?  I came home with the raffle ticket but nothing else, and of course it was not the winning one.  I thought I might make it when we meet at mine on Tuesday 3 November, though that is an ambitious thought for a man who bought his last cake in a tin.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

Hamish, guilty, that was me. I think there was a slip by the tin that said ground almonds but that's all I remember.

Kerry, sorry to put cake on the reception email. Do you still have the recipe slip from the coffee morning? Hamish (copied in) wants to bake it for our book club.

Thanks,
Luis

Dear Mr Cordero,

The slip is still at reception. It says 180g ground almonds, three pears, and 40 minutes at 170C in a 20cm tin. One of the volunteers brought it in. I don’t have the rest of the recipe.

Kind regards,

Kerry Simmonds
Reception, Whitlock Cut Dental
8 Wilton Way, London E8 1BG | 020 7946 0745
Please give 48 hours' notice of cancellations or a £35 fee applies.

Dear Luis,

The pears have it, then.  I shall make my usual almond sponge and put the three pears in it.  I had imagined doing a dry run and bringing the results on the bus for you to inspect, but on sober reflection this is how one winds up being the man on the 19 with a cake on his knees.

Many thanks to Miss Simmonds.  Please tell her I shall leave the practice in peace.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather
sounds right. maybe stick a little note by it saying almonds, in case anyone's allergic

The blue bag is mine, so no rush getting it back. It's the thick one with the split in the handle.

I'd get the damp ones out of it tonight if anyone's passing. Hang them over the backs of the chairs and leave the dry ones folded on the table. I took one out when we packed up on Saturday and you could have wrung it out.

Once they're clean, could we not turn them into a box of spares anyone can help themselves to? Last time we did that half of them went home and didn't come back. If someone needs one for a race, put their name and size in the race book and hand it over at the start.

Harriet

Harriet Lowe MCSP
Dalston Step Clinic, Dalston

Eddie

happy to take the lot home and wash them if someone can work out what temperature

Luis

I have found this key in the bottom of the umbrella stand.  In case you are wondering why I was looking there, I had lost the little key to my bike lock, which it is not. could be the bike store key from ours, we've been one short since September. does the collar have a B on it?

Could you come round with your spare and compare the two?  I am out a good deal next week, but Tuesday 27 October after four would suit.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather
